what_it_does: 5G millimeter-wave power amplifiers must send highly complex wireless signals (containing rapid on-off bursts and many signal levels) efficiently. These signals have a high peak-to-average power ratio—the peak uses far more power than the average—so running at full power all the time wastes energy. This paper describes a symbol-power-tracking supply modulator that adjusts the power amplifier's voltage 400 million times per second, responding to each transmitted symbol rather than the continuous envelope, enabling higher bandwidth support than traditional envelope-tracking approaches. An adaptive biasing network tweaks transistor operating points in real-time to maintain efficiency across varying power levels.
